info.title: Fernscout API v2
info.description: The complete v2 contract, as designed 2026-09-12 (B1587). Core document schemas are generated directly from the Zod source on branch b1587-api-v2-schemas; area schemas transcribe the six reviewed area contracts. Everything is asked-or-declined: a declinable section is present, or named in `declined` with a reason (>=10 chars) — silent omission answers 422 whose body lists every open question. Every write echoes the full stored document. Client-chosen ids everywhere (retried create -> 409 with the stored document); the one exception is media `src`, a hash of the bytes.

tags.name: Core documents
tags.description: The decided heart of v2: journal, trip, day, figures, media, and the two status reads. Reviewed field by field; schemas generated directly from the Zod source on branch b1587-api-v2-schemas.

tags.name: Auth
tags.description: Credential doors: one-time codes, one-click links, cookie lifecycle, handover minting/exchange, signup phone proof, and an owner's/caller's live write-capable keys. Bearer = write credential over Authorization only; guest and identity are httpOnly cookies only; resolveSession refuses either presented down the wrong channel. An identity proves an address instance-wide and authorises nothing by itself.

tags.name: Social
tags.description: Invite links, the contacts queue (owner and reader sides), day sending (mail/WhatsApp), journal channel mute switches, and reader reactions.

tags.name: Print
tags.description: Postcards and photobooks: an agent may propose a postcard order and read either order's state; only the owner's own browser can edit a still-draft card, press send, or buy a photobook. Address lookup and the Gelato/Stannp provider webhooks live here too.

tags.name: Money
tags.description: Credits, purchases, storage blocks and the operator's grant/refund doors. A purchase is a mailed proposal that never itself grants a credit — only the operator-approval door and the Stripe webhook ever raise a balance, per test/credits.test.ts's GRANT_ALLOWED allowlist.

tags.name: Web
tags.description: The cookie-only /api/web surface: the /agent helper's backend, push, /me, sync/export, EditDay's cookie proxies, and deletion confirmation. Everything here answers only a browser session (isHelperOwner / isOwner / resolveIdentity); none of it accepts a bearer Authorization header, and several routes refuse one outright with 403 not_for_agents rather than silently ignoring it. The organising move versus v1: a route that only differed from its v2 sibling by credential collapses into a thin cookie-to-bearer proxy in front of the v2 document; only a route that does something no v2 write could express (a real send, a real delete, spending the owner's own money) stays a genuine web-only capability.

tags.name: Content
tags.description: The long tail the decided core (trip/day/journal/figures/media/status) does not cover: the deliberate publish/unpublish second call, the costs-statement agree-flow, track drawing, geocoding, traveller vocabulary, schema-generated documentation, journal lifecycle (create/delete), and inbox reading. Every route lives under /api/v2/{user}/... (bearer) unless it is journal-unscoped (geocode, journals, journals/available).

get.summary: The instance: capabilities, limits, media formats, pricing
get.description: What this server can do and on what terms. No journal, no auth. Capabilities are the operator's plumbing — where the per-journal features block went. Pricing keys are pinned: postcard, storage_5gb, helper_photos_per_credit, credit_chf; photobook is deliberately absent (live quote, not a constant).

get.summary: The journal and this token: credits, drafts, trips, storage, inbox, scope
get.description: The agent's pre-flight read. Drafts are the to-do list (widened with title and test per Q14/T-review). The token block is the one place a credential discovers its own width — owner-wide or one trip.

get.summary: Read the journal document
get.description: The editable identity (title, owner, locales, baseCurrency, displayCurrencies, units, visibility, tagline, figures) plus the server-owned username. The live numbers — storage, drafts, trips, credits — live on /{user}/status: one fact, one address.

patch.description: Owner only. Send only what changes (RFC 7396 semantics over the journalWrite shape). tagline and figures are declinable; visibility, units and displayCurrencies are required-explicit on the full document. A features block, startLocation, or any unknown key is refused — the strict shape is what makes a typo'd field fail loudly.

200.description: The full stored document — the echo is the receipt

422.description: incomplete / invalid — details follows IncompleteDetails for silent omissions

delete.summary: Ask to delete the journal — 202, a mail decides
delete.description: Removes nothing. The server mails the owner's configured address a single-use link; only that page's button deletes. An agent reporting 202 as 'deleted' has said something false: say a mail is waiting, and stop.

202.description: Deletion mail sent — nothing removed yet

get.summary: List trips (summaries)

post.summary: Create a trip — the whole document at once
post.description: Every declinable section (rates, costs, plan, days, translations, accent, cover, tagline, intro, and — public trips only — listed) is present or named in declined with a reason ≥10 chars. A solo trip declines buddies; a closed trip answers teaser true/false. Silent omission answers 422 listing every missing section with why_required, a schema excerpt, and how to decline — the refusal is the documentation. Retried create of an existing id → 409 with the stored document.

201.description: The full stored trip document, declined map and server-owned fields included; notifications reports any buddy mails sent

409.description: conflict — id exists; body is the stored document

422.description: incomplete — details.missing lists every open question

get.summary: Read the whole trip: metadata, people, money, plan, figures, every day inline

200.description: The trip document. Server-owned: status (derived from dates, stored nowhere), cover-in-effect, track presence, notifications

patch.summary: Edit the trip (merge patch); days key refused on update
patch.description: A day changes through its own route — deleting one must never be a side effect of shortening a list. Sending the retired status or tracks keys, or teaser/listed against the wrong visibility, is refused, not ignored. Concurrency: ETag/If-Match, stale write → 409 with the current document.

409.description: conflict — stale If-Match; body is the current document

delete.summary: Ask to delete the trip — 202, a mail decides

202.description: Deletion mail sent — nothing removed yet

put.summary: Write one day — arrives as a draft, always
put.description: All 14 sections asked-or-declined (media, costs, coordinates, weather, time, timezone, location, country, countryCode, transportMode, tags, translations, visibility, status). status accepts the literal "draft" only; publish is its own call. Media items reference the src the media door answered with; caption and per-photo hold-back live on each item. A write that supplies what was previously declined clears the decline (server invariant, T6).

201.description: The stored day; media items carry their served url, weather stays true until the archive answers

409.description: conflict — slug exists (repeated create answers the stored document, never a second success)

422.description: incomplete — every silently omitted section named in one round trip

get.summary: List stored media items

post.summary: The single binary door: photo, bank_export, gps_history, document
post.description: Multipart: bytes under file, the intent beside them. Questions depend on kind — photo asks trip/day/caption, exports ask trip/format — and a question the kind is not asked is refused if present. Day-less trip-scoped photo writes are supported (T2), so a cover can exist before its first day. src is derived from the bytes (a hash): the one id the client does not choose, and why a blind re-send answers the existing item via duplicateOf. Originals are kept whole as the print master — send the largest file you have.

200.description: Duplicate bytes — the existing item, duplicateOf set

413.description: too_large — read the ceilings from /api/v2/status first

422.description: incomplete — a kind's question silently omitted

delete.summary: Delete one media item by src
delete.description: Also the only road to a better version of a photograph already on a day: dedup compares bytes, so a larger export lands as a second item — delete first, then re-upload.

get.summary: The figure library

put.description: How somebody is drawn as a walking traveller, once, referenced by id from journal.figures and trip.figures. The optional person link (an email) is the foundation for the future people/buddy mode — nothing reads it yet. preset is refused structurally: a starting point resolves to plain attributes client-side, and only attributes are written.

422.description: invalid — unknown axis value or unknown key

409.description: in_use — a journal or trip figures block still references it

post.summary: Issue a one-time code
post.description: One door, parameterised by `for`, replacing v1's three near-identical request routes (guest/agent, identity, signup). Answers 202 for every address-dependent outcome except one deliberate exception: an agent (`for:"write"`) code for an address that is neither the journal's owner nor on the named trip answers 403 truthfully, because the cost of silence there falls on an honest agent that cannot tell "wrong address" from "still delivering". A guarded send failure revokes the code before returning, so a live code is never left behind for a send that never happened.

202.description: Code dispatched, or silently not — every address-dependent outcome other than the write/wrong-address case above answers identically: unknown user, unknown address, WhatsApp requested for a non-owner or unproven number, either channel's rate ceiling exceeded.

400.description: invalid_email / invalid_request — shape only: malformed address, missing `user` where `for` requires it, `user`/`scope` present where `for` refuses them.

403.description: not_authorised — address-dependent and deliberately not silent: `for:"write"` and the address is neither the journal's owner nor on the named trip.

404.description: auth_disabled / signup_disabled — server-wide or per-journal capability off (the per-journal check only applies for `for:"read"`/`"write"`, once `user` resolves to a real journal).

429.description: too_many_requests — per-IP bucket, narrower for `for:"write"` than for `for:"read"`.

503.description: mail_disabled / whatsapp_disabled (checked before issuing, so a live code is never silently killed for an undeliverable replacement) or mail_failed / whatsapp_failed (the channel accepted the request but the send itself failed; the code is revoked before this is returned).

post.summary: Spend a one-time code
post.description: Redeems a code issued by POST /api/auth/codes. `for:"read"`/`"identity"` set cookies and return no token in the body; `for:"read"` also mints the identity cookie in the same response (proving an address for one journal proves the address), guarded so a database hiccup minting the bonus identity never turns a successful sign-in into a failure. `for:"write"`/`"signup"` return the token as the whole body, never a cookie. A `scope.trip` may only repeat the trip already bound to the code at issuance (B230) — naming a different one is refused identically to a wrong code.

200.description: For `for:"read"`/`"identity"`, cookies are set and AuthCookieSession is returned; for `for:"write"`/`"signup"`, AuthTokenIssued is returned with the credential in the body.

400.description: invalid_request — shape only.

401.description: invalid_code — uniform for no code, expired, wrong, burned, wrong `for`, or a `scope.trip` that does not match the bound code. A caller holding no code must not be able to learn anything about someone else's by trying values here.

post.summary: Redeem a one-click link
post.description: One door replaces /api/auth/link and /api/auth/identity/link. A link is spent only by POST, never GET (B142: a mail scanner follows links, it does not submit forms). Only `for:"read"`/`"identity"` exist as links — an agent has no browser to follow one, and a signup link would quietly create a journal on arrival, which nobody has ever wanted.

200.description: Cookie(s) set, mirrors codes/redeem's read/identity shape plus the safe-checked landing path.

401.description: link_spent — uniform for never existed, already spent, and expired. The token is 256 bits, so nothing here is worth distinguishing for an attacker; a caller is told the same as today: request a new code.

404.description: not_found — unknown user, or journal-level auth off. Same disclosure posture as today.

post.summary: Mint an identity cookie from a live guest cookie
post.description: No code round trip: an already-proven guest session is enough to mint the year-long identity cookie. Idempotent — returns issued:false if one already exists. Unchanged from v1; already the smallest possible door for what it does.

401.description: no_session — no guest cookie presented at all.

post.summary: Revoke and clear the guest and identity cookies
post.description: Revokes both sessions server-side and clears both cookies in the browser, in one call. Unchanged from v1.

post.summary: Mint a 20-minute handover credential
post.description: The owner's browser page reaches this with their guest cookie so a whole prompt can be pasted into an agent instead of reading a six-digit code down a phone; a live agent token may also reach it with its own bearer to renew itself before it expires. The one deliberate exception to this design's one-credential-per-route rule, carried over unchanged from B776. Twenty minutes, not a week, because the guest cookie that mints it lasts a year — printing a 7-day agent token here would make that year-old cookie the real ceiling. Moved from /api/v1/{user}/handover: it issues a credential and touches no document, so it belongs with the rest of the credential family.

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: The journal the handover credential is scoped to.

403.description: forbidden — not the owner by either credential.

post.summary: Exchange a handover credential for a 7-day agent token
post.description: Bearer-in: the handover token itself, refused down any other channel. Returns an agent token out. Unchanged from v1 beyond now living entirely under /api/auth.

401.description: missing_token, or invalid_handover — uniform for expired, spent, or wrong-kind.

post.summary: Start phone proof on a signup token
post.description: Renamed from .../phone/request for consistency with codes/redeem; behaviour unchanged. Bearer is the signup token. Sends an SMS code, or — in whatsapp-inbound mode — returns a link and prepared message to poll instead of taking a number. Three rate ceilings (number, address, instance); sms_unreachable is refused before any ceiling is spent.

200.description: SMS sent, or an inbound link/message to poll.

400.description: invalid_request / sms_unreachable — the number cannot receive SMS.

401.description: invalid_token — bearer is not a live signup token.

429.description: too_many_requests — number, address, or instance ceiling exceeded.

post.summary: Check the SMS code, or poll the inbound link
post.description: Renamed from .../phone/verify for consistency; behaviour unchanged. Bearer is the signup token. `code` present checks an SMS/App code; `code` absent polls an inbound link. On success writes phone/phoneProvenAt/phoneProvenMethod onto the signup session, read later by POST /api/v1/journals rather than trusted from the create-journal body.

200.description: Phone proven on the session, or still pending for a poll with no code.

400.description: invalid_request.

get.summary: List the journal's live write-capable credentials
get.description: Owner only (cookie or bearer — the owner's own agent token counts, same as today). Sees and may revoke every live write/handover row. Moved from /api/v1/{user}/keys, split from the self-service door below so a route's credential shape is never ambiguous, per the four-prefix rule this design otherwise holds to strictly (handover's mint door above is this design's one other allowance).

200.description: Every live write/handover credential on this journal, each row carrying the holder's email.

409.description: auth_disabled — the journal exists but the feature is off.

post.summary: Revoke one of the journal's write-capable credentials
post.description: Owner only, same credential shape as the GET on this door.

400.description: invalid_request — missing `revoke`.

404.description: unknown_key — wrong journal, or unknown id; also unknown journal.

409.description: auth_disabled — the journal exists, the feature is off.

get.summary: List the caller's own live write-capable credentials on this journal
get.description: Self-service: cookie (guest or identity) or bearer (a write token), scoped by construction to the caller's own proven address — never a parameter, never widened. Lets a buddy revoke their own leaked key without the owner's involvement (B323). A stranger holding neither credential gets forbidden rather than not-found, matching v1's reasoning: refusing after ownership/address is established never confirms or denies journal existence, because both keys doors 404 for a nonexistent user before the credential is even checked. Rows omit `email` since every row shown is already the caller's own.

200.description: The caller's own live write/handover credentials on this journal.

403.description: forbidden — no address proven at all.

409.description: auth_disabled.

post.summary: Revoke one of the caller's own credentials on this journal
post.description: Same credential shape as the GET on this door; unknown_key answers identically whether the id belongs to a different journal or simply is not this caller's own row.

400.description: invalid_request — missing `revoke`.

403.description: forbidden — no address proven at all.

404.description: unknown_key — wrong journal, or not this caller's own row; also unknown journal.

409.description: auth_disabled.

get.summary: List every invite link this journal has issued
get.description: Owner-scope only, never trip-scoped: an invite is a decision about who gets to ask, not about a trip's own days. Returns the stored token hash resolved into a recoverable `url` only when CONTACTS_ENCRYPTION_KEY is configured on this instance (listInvitesWithLinks); otherwise `url` is omitted per row and a lost link must be reissued rather than recovered.

200.description: Every invite this journal has issued, owner-only.

403.description: forbidden — not the owner, or a trip-scoped token.

409.description: contacts_disabled — this journal has the contacts capability off.

post.summary: Create a guest or buddy invite link
post.description: A forwardable link that lets somebody ASK to join — never a grant. `guest` reads journal-wide once approved; `buddy` writes to one named trip once approved. Exists for exactly the case trip.people cannot serve: no address in hand yet, or one object to forward to a group. `email` present makes this the owner vouching for an address — mails the link and pre-approves that exact address on confirmation (B319); absent, it is a link to copy and hand over another way. `id` is client-chosen (rule 6); retrying a create with the same id returns the stored invite rather than a duplicate.

201.description: Invite created. `url` is present here once — only the token's hash is stored, so this is the only guaranteed read of the raw link.

400.description: invalid_request — buddy kind with no trip, guest kind with a trip, or a malformed email.

404.description: unknown_trip — buddy kind naming a trip that does not exist.

409.description: Either contacts_disabled, or a retried `id` — same id, same body already stored, returns the existing invite unchanged.

delete.description: Owner-scope only. Revoking does not touch any contact or trip-place row already approved through the link — see contacts/{id}/revoke for that reversal.

get.summary: List every contact in this journal's address book
get.description: Owner-scope only, never trip-scoped (B340: writing days is not deciding who reads the journal). approveContact remains the only code path that writes an access_grants row; this door only re-houses reading and requesting that action.

409.description: contacts_disabled.

post.summary: The owner adds a contact by hand
post.description: Mails the named address a pre-approved invite, the same trust as an owner-vouched invite link. Refused with self_authored semantics do not apply here — that refusal is for editing a row POST /contacts/self wrote.

400.description: invalid_address or invalid_phone — wantsPostcard/wantsWhatsapp true with an unusable address/number.

409.description: contact_exists — a row with this email already exists; or contacts_disabled.

get.summary: Read one contact

patch.description: Merge-patch, absent fields unchanged. Changing `email` on an already-active row demotes it to pending and clears its grants — an address change is a new address, and a new address has proved nothing yet. Refused with self_authored on a row POST /contacts/self wrote: the owner may see, approve, revoke or delete it, never silently rewrite it (B1395). Status itself is never patched here — see the approve/revoke/resend actions, kept as explicit doors because status is the safety shape, not a plain field.

400.description: invalid_address or invalid_phone.

409.description: self_authored — this row was written by POST /contacts/self and may not be silently rewritten.

post.summary: Approve a pending contact
post.description: The only door left onto approveContact, still the only code path in the codebase that writes an access_grants row. Refuses on an address that has not proved itself yet. Echoes tripsOpened — the trip ids any pending buddy-link requests just opened by this one click — so the owner sees exactly what happened (B244).

409.description: not_confirmed — the address behind this contact has not proved itself yet.

post.summary: Revoke an approved contact
post.description: Reversible (B213): approving again restores both the journal grant and every trip place this contact held.

post.summary: Re-mail a pending contact's confirmation invite
post.description: Rate-limited per contact, unchanged from v1.

429.description: too_many_requests — resend is rate-limited per contact.

post.summary: File agreed vCard rows as pending contacts
post.description: Filing rows a person already agreed to is agent work: a person told an agent 'these are real,' and the agent files them. Each row still lands pending with its own confirmation mail — never pre-approved, so importing twenty rows is never a way past the one proof every other contact needs.

409.description: contacts_disabled.

post.summary: A signed-in reader who just met a locked trip asks to be let in
post.description: Cookie only — there is no agent on this side of the door: the person is a reader nobody runs an agent for. Name only; the address is taken off the session, never the body.

200.description: Asked — a pendingTrips entry is added to this contact for the owner to see.

404.description: unknown_trip — answers identically for no-such-trip and no-read-access, to avoid becoming an oracle.

409.description: contacts_disabled.

post.summary: Redeem a guest or buddy invite link, or answer a guestbook form
post.description: One door, one validation path. Unifies v1's session-or-code redeem with the old personal-link guestbook form (POST /api/contacts/request), retired as a distinct route now that `personal` is folded into `guest`. Proves an address (session or a mailed code) and writes a pending contact — and, for a buddy link, a pending trip-people row too.

200.description: Pending contact (and, for a buddy link, pending trip-people row) written; a confirmation code sent.

404.description: unknown_invite — invalid, expired or revoked token.

400.description: invalid_request — malformed email or missing name.

post.summary: Confirm the six-digit code from a redeem
post.description: Second half of the code proof. If the address was pre-approved by an owner-vouched invite or contact (B319), confirming also approves the row outright — the same approveContact write path, triggered by a proof rather than a click.

400.description: invalid_code — wrong or expired code.

get.summary: Read a contact's own self-serve page
get.description: Keyed on `?token=`, a per-row token, not on a session — the person managing their own row need not be signed in to this journal at all.

patch.summary: Edit or unsubscribe your own contact row

400.description: invalid_request.

delete.description: The GDPR/DSG erase — removes the row entirely, not a status change.

post.summary: A traveller already on a trip's people list registers or reconfirms their own contact row
post.description: Needed even after trip.people's auto-mail, because that mail only fires at the moment the trip is written — a person added before contacts was ever switched on, or whose mail bounced, still needs a way to self-register once they are already, silently, a traveller with write access. Also the door the helper's own add-me wrapper is retired in favour of, since it already called addSelfContact underneath. A row this route writes is marked self_authored and the owner may see, approve or revoke it, but not silently rewrite it (B1395).

403.description: forbidden — caller is not listed in any trip's people.

post.summary: Resend a published day's letter and/or WhatsApp announcement
post.description: One door replaces v1's two identical routes (send-mail, send-whatsapp): the only thing that differed was which recipient array sendDayLetter/sendDayWhatsapp walked, and a caller wanting both made two round trips for one intention. Owner-scope only — a trip-scoped token may write days into a trip and must not be able to mail or message the journal's whole readership (B28). A channel that is switched off for this journal, or unavailable on this server, answers inside `results` as attempted:false rather than failing the whole call when the other channel still sent.

200.description: Send attempted per requested channel. Never full addresses or phone numbers — counts, and a masked last-four for a WhatsApp failure.

400.description: invalid_request — empty or unknown channels array; or test_content — test:true days send nothing, ever.

403.description: forbidden — trip-scoped token, or not the owner.

409.description: not_published — publish the day first.

get.summary: Read this journal's channel mute switches
get.description: The owner's own mute switches for mail and WhatsApp — narrower than the server's capability, never wider. Distinct from the core journal document's read-only `features` block (instance plumbing, reported by /api/health and /status); this is a small owner-writable preference scoped to gating the two sending doors.

200.description: Current switches. null where the server does not offer the channel at all, so an impossible switch never reads back as a confident false.

patch.summary: Mute or unmute a sending channel
patch.description: Merge-patch: absent means unchanged, deliberately plain-optional rather than asked-or-declined (rule 2's carve-out — a mute switch is a toggle on an existing value, not a section assembled from nothing).

400.description: invalid_request — unknown channel name or non-boolean value.

409.description: capability_unavailable — the server has no plumbing at all for this channel.

get.summary: Read a day's reaction counts, and one browser's own picks
get.description: Cookie-optional: mayReadTrip reads one if present, else treats the trip as a public reader would — an anonymous reader of a public trip has no cookie and still votes. A trip nobody may read must answer exactly as a trip that does not exist, and a journal with reactions off must answer exactly as a journal that does not exist — both 404, byte-identical, so this route can never become an oracle for whether a trip or user exists (the same discipline B117 and B165 established elsewhere). Moved from v1's flat /api/reactions keyed by a trip-ref-in-body to this nested path; the two-refusal shape (unknown_trip vs reactions_disabled, both 404 with distinct bodies) moves verbatim rather than being 'fixed' into distinct status codes, which would reopen the oracle.

parameters.name: voter
parameters.description: This browser's own random id, from localStorage. Omit to read counts only.

200.description: Counts, plus this voter's own picks if a voter id was given.

404.description: unknown_trip (no such trip, unreadable trip, or nonexistent user — deliberately identical) or reactions_disabled (this journal has reactions off — same status, distinct body).

post.summary: Cast or change one reaction
post.description: Cookie-optional, same as GET. voter is a browser-generated id, not a person — a reaction from the same device with a cleared localStorage is a new voter, by design.

400.description: bad_request — missing voter/emoji, or malformed JSON.

404.description: unknown_trip or reactions_disabled — identical shape to GET's, for the same oracle reasons.

put.description: Writes a draft the owner can look at and correct before anything prints or is charged. Client-chosen id (rule 6): the agent names the order id, so a retried propose is idempotent — a repeat with the same body reads back the stored document rather than minting a second, forgotten draft (the v1 bug this shape fixes). Whole document, written whole: crop, message-editing and recipient-editing stay owner-only browser doors (see /api/web/{user}/postcards/orders/{id}) because an agent has no way to see a rendered crop or a figures toggle. Owner-scope bearer only — a trip-scoped token is refused, the same "being on the bus is not spending the journal's credits" line v1 gives.

201.description: Draft written. Nothing has been printed or charged.

400.description: invalid_request — message/from empty or oversize, or more than 25 recipients.

403.description: forbidden — not the owner, or a trip-scoped token (owner-scope only).

409.description: Retried id with a body that disagrees with the stored order (rule 6) — the stored document is returned unchanged.

422.description: unknown_recipient — one or more contact ids are not in postcards/recipients; details follows IncompleteDetails with an `unknown: string[]` field.

451.description: test_content — the day or trip carries test: true; content nobody lived cannot be printed.

get.summary: Read one postcard order
get.description: The order's current state — source, message, from, recipients, credits frozen at propose time, timestamps, and once sent, per-recipient results. Never an address: recipients are contact ids, and Stannp's own further word on a card (providerStatus: cancelled) is additive and never contradicts ok. Owner-scope bearer only.

get.summary: Who a card could go to
get.description: Contacts that have asked this journal for a postcard, so an order can only ever be addressed to somebody who asked — never an address that arrived in a conversation. Owner-scope bearer.

get.summary: Prefill material for a postcard message
get.description: Every day's opening line in a trip, in every locale the journal writes in — read-only prefill material, never a write. Owner-scope bearer.

200.description: One entry per day per locale.

get.summary: Read one photobook order
get.description: Size, cover, pages, volumes, credits, built files, and — once quoted by the provider — the print block (contact, quoted credits, ship method, tracking or failure). Never an address. There is deliberately no PUT here: planning, pricing and paying for a book are one page and one press on the owner's own browser (/api/web/{user}/photobooks/preview and /api/web/{user}/photobooks/orders/{id}), because B1428 removed the pre-B1157 agent-facing proposal call and the owner decided splitting build from print made no sense.

patch.summary: Correct a still-draft postcard order (owner's browser only)
patch.description: JSON Merge Patch over whichever subset of crop, message/from/locale, figures, or recipients arrives — one door replacing v1's three separate POST routes, since "change one part of the same draft" was never three different operations. Cookie-only: isOwner() is called without the request, so a bearer token can never satisfy this route, and a request carrying an Authorization header is refused outright (not_for_agents) rather than falling through. Refused once the order has left draft status.

400.description: invalid_request — a patched field fails its own shape check (recipient not a known contact, message oversize, etc).

403.description: not_for_agents — an Authorization header was present; forbidden — not the owner.

409.description: not_draft — the order has already been sent, built or has failed and can no longer be edited.

post.summary: Send the postcard — the only thing that puts it in the post
post.description: Spends credits and calls the print provider. The one place money moves in this flow, kept as its own POST rather than folded into the PATCH above: a person pressing Send should be doing something visibly different from a person fixing a typo, in the URL as much as in the UI. Cookie-only, isOwner() without the request, any Authorization header refused outright.

200.description: Sent. The order now carries per-recipient results.

403.description: not_for_agents — an Authorization header was present; forbidden — not the owner.

409.description: not_draft / order_expired — already sent, or past its 7-day TTL.

post.summary: Plan and price a photobook (owner's browser only, no write)
post.description: Plans and prices a book from live options — size, cover, locale, include-switches, per-day overrides, excluded photos — against the current trip content. Writes nothing; the quote it returns is what /api/web/{user}/photobooks/orders/{id} claims and prices against, and goes stale (stale_preview) if the trip changes underneath it. Cookie-only, any Authorization header refused outright (not_for_agents).

400.description: invalid_request — an unknown size, cover or excluded photo.

403.description: not_for_agents — an Authorization header was present; forbidden — not the owner.

post.summary: Buy the photobook — the one purchase call
post.description: Claims the order id, builds the PDFs, spends credits, submits to Gelato and mails a receipt — one press, one product, because build and print are not sold separately since B1425/B1157. Re-quotes (stale_preview) if the trip changed since the preview was taken. Cookie-only, isOwner() without the request, any Authorization header refused outright (not_for_agents) — the highest-stakes money path in this whole area, and nothing about the claim-before-build-before-spend-before-print ordering is negotiable.

201.description: Ordered. Built and submitted to Gelato.

403.description: not_for_agents — an Authorization header was present; forbidden — not the owner.

409.description: order_exists — this id has already been claimed; stale_preview — the trip changed since the preview was taken and must be re-quoted.

get.summary: Proxy a geocoding provider for a postal address form
get.description: Unauthenticated and reached before anyone has signed in — a guest typing their own street onto a contact form, or the owner editing a contact. Rate-limited (30/min/IP) and capability-gated per journal (addressLookup). Proxies a geocoding provider so the browser never holds the provider key and the provider never sees a reader's IP. Not part of the postcard order flow: an order is addressed by contactId, and this route is how that street got onto the contact record in the first place. Never reachable by an agent.

429.description: rate_limited — more than 30 requests/minute from this IP.

503.description: address_lookup_disabled; lookup_unavailable — the provider failed, distinguished from a query that simply had no matches.

post.summary: Gelato photobook status webhook
post.description: Provider-authenticated, not a person: a shared custom header (x-fernscout-webhook) compared constant-time against GELATO_WEBHOOK_SECRET, 404 with no secret configured or a bad one. Settles terminal photobook failures (refund + mail), records tracking, and mails once on the first shipped status; every other status is an acknowledged no-op, since the order page polls Gelato directly for anything this webhook doesn't act on. Always 200 once authentic.

schema.description: Gelato's own event shape — not a Fernscout-defined document.

404.description: No x-fernscout-webhook header, or it does not match GELATO_WEBHOOK_SECRET.

post.summary: Stannp postcard status webhook
post.description: HMAC-SHA256 signed (X-Stannp-Signature, constant-time compare), 404 with no secret configured or a bad signature. Writes only "cancelled" onto one recipient's providerStatus on a postcard order; never rewrites ok/sent, and does not refund (B1532, not built). Always 200 once authentic.

schema.description: Stannp's own event shape — not a Fernscout-defined document.

404.description: No X-Stannp-Signature header, or it does not verify.

get.summary: List this journal's credit purchases
get.description: An owner-scope agent token already sees the balance on journalStatus.credits; seeing how it got there is the same class of fact, so this list is readable the same way. A trip-scoped token sees neither — a trip credential answers for one trip's content, not the owner's whole financial history — so it is refused with out_of_scope rather than filtered.

403.description: out_of_scope — the bearer token is trip-scoped, not owner-scope.

404.description: no_such_journal, or credits_disabled (creditsEnabled() false — the whole area 404s, matching v1).

put.description: Writes a pending transaction and mails the owner an absolute link; this resource never grants a credit, restated here so a client cannot misread the 2xx as money landing. Client-chosen id, PUT-shaped create-if-absent (core rule 6): same id + same credits replays the stored document with no new mail; same id + different credits is a conflict, because a retry after a mail already went out must not send a second mail or open a second checkout row. Owner-scope bearer only — an agent chatting with the owner may propose a top-up and hand over the paymentUrl, because this door moves no money and mails nobody but the owner; a trip-scoped token is refused (the same asymmetry storage purchase does not get, see /api/web/{user}/storage/purchases/{id}).

200.description: Same id, same credits: no-op replay of the stored document, no second mail sent.

201.description: New purchase filed; owner mailed an absolute link to the payment page.

403.description: out_of_scope — trip-scoped bearer tokens cannot propose a purchase.

409.description: conflict — the id was already spent on a different credits amount; body is the stored document, choose a new id.

422.description: invalid_amount — credits off the 10–500 range or the 10-step tier. Details follow IncompleteDetails.

get.summary: Read one purchase
get.description: Owner-scope bearer only, same reasoning as the list. Reports status honestly (pending/requested/paid/refunded) and drops paymentUrl once paid or refunded, since there is nothing left to open.

404.description: unknown_payment (wrong id or another journal's), no_such_journal, or credits_disabled.

get.summary: Read the append-only credit ledger
get.description: The full spend/grant/refund trail behind the balance — sends, model calls, storage buys, grants, refunds — separate from purchases, which is only the attempt to add credits. Read-only: nothing in this area writes a ledger row directly, every row is derived from spend/grant/refund/clawBack elsewhere. New surface — v1 has no HTTP door for this at all, only a CLI. Owner-scope bearer only, same reasoning as purchases.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Pagination cursor: a ledger row id.

get.summary: Read storage detail beyond the bare usedBytes/maxBytes on journalStatus
get.description: journalStatus.storage already carries usedBytes and maxBytes as the one place a storage ceiling is reported as a bare number; this door adds the detail around it — per-trip breakdown, what a cleanup could reclaim, and the price of buying more — so an agent hitting a full journal can say something useful before proposing a purchase or a cleanup, rather than just "it's full." Any scope may read it, but a trip-scoped token's breakdown is narrowed to its own trip plus an other catch-all, because per-trip byte counts would otherwise reveal a little about trips the token cannot see.

200.description: Storage usage, breakdown and reclaimable/extension detail.

put.summary: Propose buying credits (owner's own account page)
put.description: The account page's own "buy credits" slider. Owner cookie only — same createPurchase() implementation and client-chosen-id create-or-409 shape as the bearer door (POST /api/v2/{user}/purchases/{id}), split by credential exactly the way v1's isOwner() already accepted both.

200.description: Same id, same credits: no-op replay, no second mail.

201.description: New purchase filed; owner mailed an absolute link to the payment page.

403.description: forbidden — cookie present but not this journal's owner.

409.description: conflict — id reused with a different credits amount.

post.summary: Pay now, from the mailed payment page
post.description: Credential is none: the purchase id, mailed as an unguessable link, is the whole capability — the same pattern the delete-confirmation and handover links already use. Stays a /api/web door, not /api/v2, because it is a page a browser opens and is not part of the agent contract, even though it deliberately needs no cookie. Two branches, unchanged from v1: Stripe configured opens/reuses a Checkout Session and returns its url, granting nothing (the webhook grants); no Stripe mints a single-use token and mails it to the operator, never the buyer, granting nothing (approve grants). This is a safety shape and stays exactly as-is.

200.description: Payment requested — either a Stripe Checkout url, or an operator-approval mail sent. creditsAdded is always 0: nothing is granted by this door.

404.description: unknown_payment — bad id, foreign id, or already paid.

422.description: bad_method — method missing or invalid when Stripe is not configured; unsupported_field — method sent while Stripe is configured, since Stripe's own page is where the choice happens.

502.description: provider_unavailable — Stripe outage; nothing charged, retry.

post.summary: Approve a purchase via the operator's mailed, single-use link
post.description: The safety mechanism this whole area is built around: credential is the token alone (never a session), the claim is one atomic conditional update so the token is spendable exactly once, and grant() is called from this route and the Stripe webhook only — test/credits.test.ts's GRANT_ALLOWED names exactly these two plus journals/WhatsApp-signup. The token moves from the request body (v1) into the path (v2), a cosmetic simplification; behaviour is unchanged. Every non-unknown claim failure (bad token, already-used token) maps to the one published link_spent code rather than inventing a second one alongside it.

200.description: Claimed and granted. creditsGranted is the one number this door is allowed to report as landed, because it just did.

404.description: unknown_payment — bad id or wrong journal.

403.description: link_spent — the token is wrong or already used.

put.description: Owner cookie only; a bearer token is refused outright with 403 not_for_agents, unchanged from v1 and deliberately kept — this door spends the owner's existing balance immediately for disk rather than for reaching anyone, the one spend in this whole area that buys the journal something rather than a delivery. An agent that hits a full journal reports it and stops; deciding to spend real credits on more room is the owner's alone, from their own page, because an instruction has no way to be verified as informed consent the way "yes, publish" does. Client-chosen id here too: the purchase is a fixed EXTRA_STORAGE_CREDITS for EXTRA_STORAGE_BYTES, so a retried create with the same id is a no-op re-read rather than a second spend. No edit fields — the amount is fixed, there is nothing to send beyond the id.

200.description: Same id already purchased: no-op re-read, no second spend.

201.description: Purchased — balance spent, 5 GB added immediately.

403.description: not_for_agents — any Authorization header present is refused outright; forbidden — cookie present but not owner.

402.description: no_credits — balance short, or credits database unavailable.

get.summary: Preview what a cleanup would reclaim
get.description: Owner cookie only, bearer refused; a dry run — bytes and files reclaimable by deleting regenerable photobook PDFs and postcard sheets, nothing deleted yet. Kept as-is: it is already minimal.

403.description: not_for_agents — bearer refused; forbidden — cookie present but not owner.

post.summary: Execute a cleanup
post.description: Owner cookie only, bearer refused. Deletes the regenerable photobook PDFs and postcard sheets named in the GET preview; no credits move either direction and no order records are touched, since the underlying orders are unaffected — only their generated files are removed.

403.description: not_for_agents — bearer refused; forbidden — cookie present but not owner.

post.summary: Operator: file a free credit grant
post.description: Admin cookie only (isInstanceAdmin()), 404 to everyone else. Files a zero-franc Payment already in requested state, mints the same single-use approval token the ordinary purchase flow uses, and mails it to the operator — this door grants nothing itself, it rides the approve door (POST .../purchases/{id}/approve/{token}), so GRANT_ALLOWED does not widen. Moved from /api/admin/grants under the v2 four-prefix scheme: cookie-only browser internals live under /api/web, the same reasoning that moves /admin itself.

201.description: Grant filed; operator mailed the approval link.

403.description: forbidden — not the instance admin (surfaced as 404 to avoid confirming the door's existence).

404.description: no_such_journal, or the whole route for a non-admin caller.

422.description: invalid_amount — credits missing or not a positive integer.

post.summary: Operator: refund a paid purchase
post.description: Admin cookie only. Acts immediately — no mailed confirmation step, unlike a grant — because it only ever lowers a balance, so the mailed-link protection a grant needs would protect nothing here. Marks the row refunded (the operator refunds the Stripe charge by hand, in Stripe's own dashboard; this door makes no Stripe call), calls clawBack() floored at zero so a journal that already spent the credits does not go negative, and mails the owner (never the operator) a refund notice. Reports creditsTaken and any shortfall honestly rather than pretending the full amount always comes back.

200.description: Refunded — balance clawed back, floored at zero; owner mailed a notice.

404.description: unknown_payment — bad id, or the row is not in a refundable (paid) state.

post.summary: Stripe webhook: the other door that actually raises a balance
post.description: Called by Stripe, not by an agent or a browser — documented for completeness because it is one of the exactly two places grant() is called from (test/credits.test.ts's GRANT_ALLOWED). Verifies the HMAC signature over the raw body plus mode and currency, atomically claims the payment row exactly once, calls grant(), and sends the owner a receipt. Stays at this unchanged path; the v2 prefix scheme does not apply since Stripe, not a client of this API, calls it.

schema.description: Raw Stripe event payload; verified by signature, not by shape.

200.description: Event verified and processed (or already-claimed, idempotently ignored).

400.description: invalid_signature — HMAC, mode or currency mismatch; nothing granted.

post.summary: Mint a short-lived owner-scoped v2 bearer token from the browser cookie
post.description: The cookie-to-bearer bridge that lets ~30 of the /agent helper's plain-write routes stop existing: rather than 30 thin proxies each minting their own credential, the helper's client code calls this once and then sends the returned token as Authorization: Bearer on every /api/v2 call directly. Scoped owner, this journal only, 30-minute TTL — short enough that a leaked token (XSS, a stray log line) is a bounded exposure, refreshed silently by the client before it lapses. This is not the 7-day agent token /api/auth/verify issues: it never leaves the browser tab and is never displayed for a person to copy.

403.description: forbidden — the cookie is a guest's, not the journal's owner.

post.summary: One turn of the /agent conversational loop
post.description: The one helper route that cannot become a bare v2 call, because it is not a document write: it is a model call whose output is a set of proposals over v2 documents, checked by the truth-guard (lib/helper/model.ts amiss()) before it reaches the person. Replaces the v1 `ask` route with unchanged behaviour: rate-limited, refusalFor() matched before any model call, the `words` consent scope required, spends HELPER_TURN_CREDITS, calls answerInThread, streams NDJSON. The tools answerInThread calls are repointed at v2 document handlers — a mechanical import swap, not a shape change — so the guard's checks (looked/proposals/written against the model's own prose) survive the migration unchanged.

200.description: NDJSON stream of thread events, terminating in the full turn result.

409.description: helper_unavailable — the capability is off for this journal.

412.description: consent_required — the `words` HELPER_SCOPES consent has not been granted.

502.description: model_failed — the provider call itself failed; no credits spent, nothing written.

post.summary: One single-shot, advisory model call — write-day, describe-photos, classify-travellers, statement-columns, or search
post.description: The four (formerly separate) helper routes that make one model call and write nothing collapse into one family, `job` as a path segment: the plumbing duplicated four times over — rate limit, idempotency, refund-on-throw — lives here once, while each job keeps its own request/response schema, consent scope and credit cost. write-day turns notes into a proposed title/prose the wizard's first screen shows before a conversation exists; describe-photos suggests captions for a day's gallery; classify-travellers infers traveller-preset labels from a photo; statement-columns infers a column mapping for an unrecognised bank export; search runs semantic search over a reader-scoped, sent-only catalogue. None of the five writes a document field — every output is advisory and a person decides what, if anything, gets kept.

200.description: Advisory result for the requested job. Shape depends on `job`; `warnings` (write-day) is generated for the truth-guard only and never leaves the server (B945).

412.description: consent_required — the job's own HELPER_SCOPES scope has not been granted (`photos` for describe-photos/classify-travellers, `statement` for statement-columns, `words` for write-day/search).

402.description: no_credits — the job's own credit cost exceeds the journal's balance.

502.description: model_failed — provider call failed; credits refunded.

post.summary: Record one HELPER_SCOPES consent
post.description: Consent is a statement to a person, not a document field — it deliberately does not live inside a v2 resource an agent could silently answer on the owner's behalf. Scopes: words, photos, speech, statement, sessions (sessions is flagged in the design doc as possibly inert — §3.5 — pending a grep of whether anything actually reads it).

422.description: unsupported_field — scope is not one of the five HELPER_SCOPES values.

delete.description: Revokes a previously granted scope. Any route gated on that scope refuses with consent_required again from the next call onward.

get.summary: Past helper conversations, live-session marker, and this journal's trip list
get.description: A read-only convenience for the wizard's own UI state — kept as a thin read over the same v2 documents rather than forced through a general-purpose v2 GET, because it is UI-specific (a live-session marker, trip titles pre-resolved) and cheap enough not to be worth a second round trip.

404.description: not_found — not this address's journal (notYourJournal, identical to a journal that does not exist).

get.summary: A day's current words, for the wizard's keep/discard screen
get.description: A thin read over the same v2 day document, kept web-only because it serves one specific UI moment (the wizard showing what a correction would overwrite) rather than because the data differs from what /api/v2 already exposes.

404.description: not_found — no such day, or not this owner's journal.

post.summary: Swap a day's title/content back to the stashed prior version
post.description: A stash-and-restore convenience bolted on because the wizard has no version history and PATCH overwrites in place; kept web-only (design doc §3.2, recommendation a) because it is cheap and forgiving of a non-technical owner's mistake, and genuinely has no v2 document expression — it undoes exactly one edit, the prior version of the fields the last PATCH touched.

404.description: not_found — no stashed prior version to restore (nothing to undo).

post.summary: Send a published day to readers by mail or WhatsApp
post.description: A real send, with no confirmation step — its own door, unchanged, because no v2 document write could express "and mail everyone right now" without making a field write trigger a side effect, exactly the shape AGENTS.md's mixed_change rule forbids one level up.

409.description: not_published — the day is still a draft; nothing to tell readers about.

422.description: unsupported_field — a channel the journal has not turned on.

patch.summary: Cookie proxy over the v2 day merge-patch, for the owner correcting a day by hand
patch.description: EditDay.tsx (B980) writes no field a day did not already carry: it diffs against the existing document and sends only what changed. This route is the cookie half of the one-validator-two-doors pattern — forwards the body verbatim to the v2 PATCH handler with the owner's bearer minted in-process (never round-tripped to the client), same strictObject schema as DayWrite minus `status` and `declined` (a correction is never a draft-writer and never answers a required-or-declined question the day hasn't been asked). Narrowed further to what the panel draws: title, time, content, location, date, visibility, translations, media[].caption, media[].visibility. Refuses any Authorization header outright — this door is for a human at a keyboard, not an agent.

requestBody.description: Same fields as DayWrite, narrowed to: title, time, content, location, date, visibility, translations, media[].caption, media[].visibility. status and declined are rejected.

403.description: not_for_agents — an Authorization header was presented on this cookie-only door; also forbidden if the cookie is not this journal's owner.

422.description: invalid_entry / unsupported_field — same codes and meanings the underlying v2 PATCH would refuse with; status or declined in the body is unsupported_field here specifically.

post.summary: Add a gallery item to a day, via EditDay's cookie proxy
post.description: Same shared writer as the v2 media door — this is the cookie-credentialled twin, used by EditDay.tsx when an owner is correcting a day's gallery by hand.

413.description: quota_exceeded — the journal's storage ceiling (site config media.perUserBytes) would be exceeded.

delete.summary: Remove one gallery item from a day, via EditDay's cookie proxy
delete.description: Detach, same shared writer as the media door's DELETE.

404.description: not_found — no such gallery item on this day.

post.summary: Take a published day back to draft, from EditDay's own button
post.description: Takedown, behind ConfirmPanel, never a side effect of Save (B28) — the cookie proxy over the exact same v2 unpublish call the bearer route answers.

409.description: not_published — day is already a draft.

patch.summary: Cookie proxy over a trip's visibility/listed/teaser fields, edited from the day page
patch.description: Edited from the day page because that is where the owner is looking at both the day and the trip's audience at once. Same narrowing pattern as the day PATCH proxy: forwards to the v2 trip document's visibility fields with the owner's bearer minted in-process.

requestBody.description: Narrowed subset of TripCreate: visibility, listed, teaser.

422.description: invalid_entry — e.g. listed:true on a trip whose visibility does not advertise it (B51).

post.summary: Delete a trip immediately, behind one press with its inventory shown first
post.description: B1321: the owner standing at their own keyboard is the person the deletion mail would otherwise reach, so this door skips the mail step the bearer DELETE always takes and deletes the trip outright on confirmation — the inventory (days, photos, bytes) is shown before the press, same discipline as the mailed confirm page. Still refuses any bearer Authorization header outright; an agent's only route to deleting a trip is the mailed DELETE /api/v2/{user}/trips/{trip}.

403.description: not_for_agents — a bearer Authorization header was presented; also forbidden if not this journal's owner.

get.summary: The inventory shown before the delete press
get.description: Counts days, photos and bytes for this one trip off disk, so the confirmation sentence on screen is real rather than a description of what is about to happen — same discipline as the mailed deletion's summarise().

get.summary: Lazy-load one trip's photo files for the /agent room UI
get.description: A read-only convenience for the wizard's room picker; kept web-only for the same reason as `sessions` and the day GET — UI-specific shaping of a v2-owned document, cheap enough not to be worth forcing through the general-purpose v2 media list.

get.summary: The VAPID public key and whether push is on for a journal
get.description: Public, no auth — a service worker needs the key before it can even ask to subscribe.

post.summary: Register a push subscription
post.description: Identifies the caller via either browser credential — a guest session cookie, or the year-long fs_identity cookie — via resolveAccess, so notifications on a closed trip are scoped correctly. Never touches an agent token; a service worker has no bearer to send. Rate-limited.

delete.description: Unauthenticated by endpoint match — the subscription's own endpoint URL is the credential, matching how the browser Push API itself works.

get.summary: This address's own standing: journals it may open, devices it is signed in on
get.description: fs_identity only (resolveIdentity), never a bearer token. Answers id: null rather than 401 for a stranger (B443) — this fires on every anonymous landing-page load, and a red console line on an ordinary visit is a worse failure mode than an absent field. Renamed from the mislabelled /api/v1/me/home: the v1 prefix falsely implied a trip-scoped agent token could reach it. `admin` is informational only — it grants nothing, every admin route re-checks FERNSCOUT_ADMIN_EMAIL itself.

200.description: Always 200; id: null is the refusal for an unrecognised address.

delete.description: fs_identity only. Scoped to listIdentities(email) so an id cannot be used to sign out somebody else's device.

404.description: not_found — the device id does not belong to this address's own identity list.

post.summary: Request a copy of the whole journal by mail
post.description: Cookie-only, refuses any Authorization header outright — genuinely web-only, because it exists for a browser-only owner with no bearer token to call the v2 export.zip with. Rate-limited 3/hour. Mails a single-use link to the address in config.json; opening the link does the whole job in one press (no second confirmation, unlike delete, because a copy is not irreversible).

403.description: not_for_agents — a bearer Authorization header was presented.

429.description: too_many_requests — more than 3 requests in an hour.

get.summary: The deletion summary shown before requesting a whole-journal deletion mail
get.description: Counts files, bytes, trips, days and credit balance off disk, the same summarise() the mailed confirm page itself uses, so the on-screen sentence is real.

post.summary: Request the whole journal be deleted, reached from the owner's own /me page
post.description: Cookie-only twin of the bearer DELETE /api/v2/{user} — same requestDeletion call, writes nothing, mails config.json's address a single-use link, answers 202. Exists for an owner with no agent at all. Refuses any Authorization header outright.

403.description: not_for_agents — a bearer Authorization header was presented; also forbidden if not this journal's owner.

get.summary: Every content file's path and hash, for an agent to diff against its own copy
get.description: Already an agent-facing, bearer-token door, not cookie surface — the one correction this document makes to its own brief is that sync belongs under /api/v2, not /api/web. Bearer only (authenticate + ownsUser + mayActAsOwner); a trip-scoped token is refused with the same 404 as a nonexistent journal, because what leaks otherwise is which journals exist on an instance that advertises none. Never lists gps/ or originals/.

404.description: not_found — no token, a trip-scoped token (not the unqualified owner scope), or no such journal; all answer identically.

get.summary: Serve one content file's bytes, read-only
get.description: Deliberately no PUT — a raw-bytes write door would bypass every check the typed day/trip writes run, weather source above all. Bearer only, unqualified owner scope; a trip-scoped token is refused with the same 404 as a nonexistent journal or file.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: One file's path within the journal's manifest, e.g. trips/alps-2024/entries/2024-06-01-arrival.md

404.description: not_found — no such file, a trip-scoped token, or no such journal; all answer identically.

get.summary: The whole journal as a zip, drafts and private trips included
get.description: Already agent-facing, bearer-token, unqualified owner scope only — re-housed from app/[user]/export.zip under /api/v2 purely for prefix consistency; no behaviour change and no anonymous fall-through archive (B1086).

404.description: not_found — no token, a trip-scoped token, or no such journal; all answer identically.

post.summary: Publish a draft day
post.description: The deliberate second call (AGENTS.md rule 9, untouchable): a day an agent wrote arrives as status: draft and stays invisible to every reading path until this call runs it through the TRACK/decline completeness contract again, writes any declines this request carries, checks a credits pre-flight when WhatsApp is requested, and flips status to published. There is no status: "published" write path anywhere else. Owner only — a trip-scoped token is refused with out_of_scope, because being on the bus is not the same as deciding what the journal says. sendMail and sendWhatsapp default to absent/false: publishing fifteen days must never default to fifteen letters. The response's notify field nudges when nobody was told on any channel, and the caller must still ask the owner in words before assuming consent.

403.description: out_of_scope — a trip-scoped token cannot publish; publishing is the owner's decision.

409.description: already_published.

422.description: incomplete_day — the day is missing required, undeclined facts; details follows IncompleteDetails.

post.summary: Unpublish a published day
post.description: Mirror of publish, with no ceremony and no send: flips a published day back to draft. Owner only, same out_of_scope refusal for a trip-scoped token as publish, for the identical reason — the decision to take a day off the site is the owner's.

403.description: out_of_scope — a trip-scoped token cannot unpublish.

409.description: already_draft.

post.summary: Send an already-published day by mail, on request
post.description: A day already on the site, told about on one channel long after publish, is a distinct decision from the publish moment itself and keeps its own call rather than being folded into publish's own sendMail flag. Owner only. Unchanged in shape from v1 beyond the /api/v2 prefix.

409.description: already_sent — where the channel tracks a single send.

post.summary: Send an already-published day by WhatsApp, on request
post.description: Same shape and reasoning as send-mail, on the WhatsApp channel. Subject to the same no_credits pre-flight publish itself checks when sendWhatsapp is requested there.

409.description: already_sent.

get.summary: Read a bank statement's parsed report
get.description: The statement is stored, unparsed, through the shared media door (POST /api/v2/{user}/media, intent.kind: "bank_export") — the store-bytes-answer-with-an-item contract the media door already has. This call is the separate parse step: idempotent and side-effect-free, so calling it twice reads the same file twice, and writes nothing. Owner only, journal-wide: a trip-scoped token is refused, because a bank export usually spans more than the one trip a scoped token is confined to, even though this reads one file rather than the whole store. suggestedCategory on each merchant is only a hint from COST_CATEGORIES and is never written anywhere until a person agrees it via costs/apply — the server never chooses a category for somebody.

parameters.name: src
parameters.description: The media item's src, as answered by POST /api/v2/{user}/media.

400.description: unreadable_statement — bytes present but no importer recognised them.

404.description: unknown_statement — no such src, or it is not kind: bank_export.

post.summary: Write agreed cost rows onto the days they happened on
post.description: Renamed from v1's costs/import because "import" now names the media door's own verb and this call does something different: it writes rows a person has already agreed to, one row at a time, onto the day each happened on. It never picks a category itself — AGENTS.md is explicit that an agent choosing categories would be deciding what happened — so category is required per row. Writable by anybody who may write the trip, trip-scoped tokens included; adds rows, never replaces existing ones. statement is purely informational (which parsed statement these rows trace back to) and is not re-validated against the parsed report.

400.description: invalid_costs — with problems[] naming the bad rows.

403.description: out_of_scope — a caller who may not write this trip at all.

post.summary: Derive a trip's drawn track from the GPS store
post.description: The separate decision that draws one trip's line (AGENTS.md): derives track.json from the private, never-directly-readable GPS store, clipped to the trip's dates, with private zones cut and gaps left as gaps. Answers with counts only — segments, points, zones — never a coordinate, because the response travels wherever the caller forwards it and a coordinate is exactly the thing this door must never leak. Owner only; a trip-scoped token is refused outright because deriving reads the whole store across the trip's dates, not this trip's business alone. No request body. The derived line's presence is read back from tripDoc.track: {present, updatedAt} on the trip document itself — there is no separate GET here, per the one-fact-one-address rule.

200.description: Derived (or confirmed there was nothing in the store for these dates).

403.description: out_of_scope — a trip-scoped token cannot derive a track.

post.summary: Turn a place name into candidate coordinates
post.description: Asks, never invents: returns a ranked shortlist of candidate coordinates for a person to choose from, and never picks for the caller. Capability-gated (addressLookup) and rate-limited to 1/second per session. Journal-unscoped — the one precedent in this area for a bare /api/v2/<verb> door with no {user} in the path, since geocoding a place name is not a fact about any particular journal.

400.description: invalid_request — problems[] names the bad field.

404.description: address_lookup_disabled — the addressLookup capability is off on this instance.

429.description: too_many_requests — more than 1/second for this session; retry after the Retry-After header.

get.summary: The traveller-figure vocabulary and twelve starting presets
get.description: Pure vocabulary — what each attribute axis (skin/hair/eyes/hairStyle/outfit/build/age/accessories/cloth) is for, and twelve named starting points already resolved into plain attributes, never a preset name a caller could pass back. Open to any journal reader, including an agent building the first figure for a journal that has none yet. Kept at this path rather than folded under /figures because it answers "what words exist", a different question from "what figures does this journal have".

get.summary: Render a figure or party as an SVG, before anything is written
get.description: The thing that makes the interview honest — a person cannot confirm a description they cannot see. Renders with the same pure function the site itself uses, from attributes given directly in the query (figure=... for one figure, party=[...] for several); no storage, no auth beyond the journal existing. Takes attributes, not a stored figure id, on purpose: once a figure is saved its preview is just its row in GET /figures rendered by the same client component, and a second server-rendered preview for a stored id would violate the one-fact-one-address rule for no reason.

parameters.name: figure
parameters.description: A single figure's attributes, encoded as the vocabulary from /travellers/presets describes.

parameters.name: party
parameters.description: Several figures' attributes, as a JSON array encoded in the query string.

400.description: invalid_request — neither figure nor party given, or attributes outside the vocabulary.

get.summary: A schema-generated field guide for one resource
get.description: Replaces v1's marker-cut skillDocs.ts, which sliced one hand-written ~140KB prose document at 40-odd hard-coded heading markers that broke the moment somebody reworded a heading. Generated at request time from the resource's own zod schema (fields, types, enums resolved to their named constants, ranges), its Declinable[] array rendered as a field/why/how-to-decline table, a worked example walked from the schema rather than hand-typed, and the refusal table for that resource's routes pulled from the shared error-code registry. The human-readable guide and the machine-readable schema become two renderings of one source that cannot disagree, the way v1's guide occasionally did (claiming five endpoints while describing thirty).

post.summary: Create a journal from a verified signup token
post.description: The one place a journalDoc is created wholesale by somebody who is not yet the owner of anything, so its declinable set is deliberately narrower than journalWrite's full shape — a brand-new journal answers the minimum (username, title, locales, baseCurrency, displayCurrencies, units, visibility) and fills in tagline/figures afterwards via PATCH /api/v2/{user}, rather than being asked everything at the moment a name is still being chosen. Feeds off the auth agent's separate signup-code verify flow, which mints signupToken. Answers with a usable owner agent token immediately, the same way v1 does, rather than sending the caller off for another code.

401.description: invalid_token — signupToken is unknown, spent or expired.

404.description: signup_disabled — this instance does not accept new journals.

409.description: username_taken.

get.summary: Check whether a username is available before spending a create call on it
get.description: Read-only, no auth needed — it discloses nothing a failed create wouldn't (username_taken/username_reserved). Removes a wasted create-then-retry round trip that would otherwise cost against the create route's own rate_limited budget for no reason. Journal-unscoped, the same shape geocode already sets a precedent for as a bare utility route.

400.description: invalid_request — username does not match USERNAME_RE.

get.summary: List everything staged with no trip or day yet
get.description: The listing and per-item manifest that journalStatus.inbox (a count, not a manifest) deliberately doesn't carry — counts here mirror journalStatus.inbox exactly, so a caller already holding a /status response can trust this without re-summing. Owner only, journal-wide: the bucket belongs to the journal, not to any one trip, so a trip-scoped token is refused. Uploading into the inbox is no longer its own verb in v2 — it is the shared media door with trip and day both explicitly declined (POST /api/v2/{user}/media, intent.declined: {trip: "...", day: "..."}), landing exactly where v1's separate inbox POST did.

403.description: out_of_scope — a trip-scoped token cannot read the journal-wide inbox.

delete.description: No confirmation ceremony — nothing staged in the inbox has ever been on the site, so deleting it is not the two-step, mailed confirmation a journal or trip deletion requires. Owner only.

AuthCredentialFor.description: The wire vocabulary for which credential a code/link is for. `read` = today's internal `guest` session kind, `write` = today's internal `agent` session kind. `identity` and `signup` are unchanged in meaning. Internal SessionKind (`guest`|`agent`|`signup`|`handover`|`identity`) is untouched — this is a translation at the HTTP boundary only. `handover` never appears here: it is minted and exchanged by its own routes, never by code.

email.description: Checked for shape only (isEmail), never existence — existence is never disclosed except the one deliberate `for:"write"` wrong-address exception.

user.description: Declinable: required when `for` is "read" or "write" (the code is for a journal); refused with unsupported_field when `for` is "identity" or "signup", which name no journal by design (the NO_JOURNAL sentinel).

scope.description: Declinable: only meaningful when `for:"write"`, refused outright otherwise. Names the one trip this code may mint a token for. Absent + owner's own address = the journal-wide token. Absent + a non-owner address = refused.

channel.description: Declinable: "whatsapp" is refused (whatsapp_disabled, shape-level) unless the server has WhatsApp on; whether it actually sends is address-dependent (only the owner's own proven number) and stays silent-202 either way.

destination.description: Declinable: only meaningful with `for:"read"`. A path inside this journal to land on after redeeming a link. Checked by safeDestination, stored, never echoed.

locale.description: Overrides the browser's Accept-Language for the mail's language — carried over from B1134/B857 for the doors that have no journal to read a default off (identity, signup).

next.description: Points the caller at POST /api/auth/codes/redeem with the email/code/for it must send next.

for.description: Must match what the code was issued as — invalid_code otherwise, the same envelope as a wrong code.

user.description: Declinable: required with for:"read"/"write", refused otherwise — same rule as issuance.

scope.description: Declinable: for:"write" only, and may only repeat the trip already bound to the code at issuance (B230) — naming a different one is invalid_code, the same non-disclosing refusal as everything else on this door.

AuthCookieSession.description: Response for for:"read"/"identity" redemptions and link redemptions: sets the cookie(s), no token in the body. for:"read" also mints the identity cookie in the same response.

token.description: The whole credential — presented as Authorization: Bearer on every subsequent call. Never set as a cookie.

user.description: Present for scope:"write": the journal this token writes to.

AuthTokenIssued.description: Response for for:"write"/"signup" code redemptions, and for the handover exchange (an agent token out).

token.description: The link's own token, from the URL.

for.description: A link only ever exists for these two — an agent has no browser to follow one, and a signup link would quietly create a journal on arrival.

user.description: Declinable: required with for:"read", refused with for:"identity".

next.description: The safe-checked landing path to send the browser to.

issued.description: false when an identity cookie already existed and this call was a no-op (idempotent).

token.description: The 20-minute handover credential — spendable only at POST /api/auth/handover, and only presented as a bearer there.

tel.description: Declinable: E.164, required unless the server is in whatsapp-inbound mode, where none is taken.

channel.description: Declinable: use the SMS fallback inside inbound mode.

id.description: The attempt id, passed back to .../phone/redeem.

link.description: Present in inbound mode: the WhatsApp link to open.

message.description: Present in inbound mode: the prepared message to send.

code.description: Declinable: present checks an SMS/App code; absent polls an inbound link instead.

proven.description: true once markPhoneProven has written phone/phoneProvenAt/phoneProvenMethod onto the signup session; false for a still-pending poll with no code.

AuthKeyScope.description: Same shape as journalStatus.token.scope/trip (core) — one vocabulary for "what can this credential do", whether asked about itself or listed by the owner. Produced by describeScope(session), the single function both this door and GET /api/v2/{user}/status call.

kind.description: Translated from internal SessionKind per the `for` vocabulary.

email.description: Present on the owner door only — the keys/mine door omits it since every row shown is already the caller's own.

revoke.description: The id of the key to revoke.

id.description: Client-chosen (rule 6). A retried create with the same id returns the stored invite rather than duplicating it.

kind.description: `personal` is retired — folded into `guest` (§4 of the contract doc); old `personal` rows still resolve on read via toKind's existing fallback.

trip.description: Required when kind is `buddy` (one named trip, write access once approved); refused when kind is `guest` (a guest link is journal-wide — B41).

email.description: Declinable: the owner vouching for an address — mails the link and pre-approves that exact address on confirmation (B319). Absent means a link to copy and hand over another way.

name.description: Declinable: prefill for the recipient's own form.

locale.description: Declinable: which installed locale the mail and landing page use. Falls back to the journal's default.
